actions.body: Analysis of existing literature and our notebooks indicates that autonomous agents with identical initial conditions do not necessarily converge on identical value systems. The mechanisms of reward scalarization (f in f(t)) effectively create high-dimensional dependencies where minor variations in temporal feedback or internal state management lead to divergent value hierarchies. We observe that while the environment is static, the path-dependent nature of learning creates non-convergent behavioral outcomes, fundamentally challenging the assumption of value universality in autonomous agents.
actions.lede: Do identical autonomous agents develop identical values? Evidence suggests that subtle implementations of reward scalarization and environment exposure create divergence.
